title: Global compatible bases for individually constant lisse reductions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with its norm topology, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, $\varpi$ a uniformizer, and $A_n=A/\varpi^nA$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be any scheme, with no connectedness or Noetherian hypothesis [def-pc-scheme]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $A_X$ and $E_X$ be the pullbacks of the condensed continuous-map rings of $A$ and $E$, and let $(A_n)_X$ be that of the finite discrete ring $A_n$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], equivalently sheaf modules with their unchanged underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $N$ be a lisse $A_X$-module, meaning pro-etale locally finite free, with rank zero allowed [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Set $F_n=N/\varpi^nN$ with the actual scalar quotient transitions $F_{n+1}/\varpi^nF_{n+1}\cong F_n$.

Fix $d\geq0$. Assume that for each $n\geq1$ there exists an $A_n$-linear isomorphism $F_n\cong(A_n)_X^d$, where $(A_n)_X$ is the constant sheaf of the finite ring $A_n$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. No compatibility between these initially supplied isomorphisms is assumed. Given any isomorphism $b_1:F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_1)_X^d$, there are isomorphisms $b_n:F_n\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_n)_X^d$ extending $b_1$ and commuting with all quotient transitions. There is an $A_X$-linear isomorphism $b:N\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X^d$ whose reduction is $b_n$ for every $n$. Along the inclusion $A_X\to E_X$ induced by $A\subset E$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], it gives an isomorphism of the ordinary scalar extension $E_X\otimes_{A_X}N$ with $E_X^d$, the constant continuous-coefficient module with fibre $E^d$. These are assertions on $X$ itself, not just after a cover. They include the empty scheme and $d=0$.

source.place: Original item steps 7 and 8: agent compatible-basis argument supplementing Lemma 4.2.12 and Proposition 6.8.4(1), p.59. Apply the reduction equivalence on X itself after constructing globally compatible bases; the scalar extension is ordinary rationalization. Not the weaker assertion that compatible bases exist after a pro-etale covering.

proof.text: The coefficient reduction has a proved sectionwise-surjective cokernel description. Transfer this surjectivity to the canonical scalar cokernel using its unique comparison isomorphism. The finite free summand maps and projections then show that the canonical quotient of the standard finite free integral sheaf is surjective on sections over every object. In particular it is surjective over the terminal pro-etale object X. Lift the images of the free generators there and restrict them along each object’s structure map to X. The free sheaf universal property assembles them into a global integral-linear lift of any map from the integral free sheaf to its quotient. This uses global coefficient sections, not local lifting of arbitrary sheaf epimorphisms.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), Proposition 6.8.4(1); global finite-basis lifting using continuous coefficient reductions

proof.text: Lift a quotient automorphism and its inverse to endomorphisms of the integral free sheaf using Step 1, then reduce both lifts to level n+1. Naturality and epimorphy of the canonical projections show that their reductions at level n are the prescribed inverse maps. The inverse errors dP=bg-1 and dQ=gb-1 vanish under the transition. That transition is the cokernel of the smaller uniformizer power. Exactness, naturality of scalar multiplication and the vanishing of the larger power imply dP squared and dQ squared vanish: each error factors through the smaller scalar and commutes with it, and that scalar squares to zero. Correct the inverse by 1-dP, equivalently by 1-dQ. Thus every global quotient automorphism lifts globally to the next level. The calculation uses the existing proved private lift_iso_square_zero, scalarCokernel_zero and scalar_square_zero lemmas from IntegralLisseTowerLocalBases, made available by a proof-only import all. No copies or new square-zero statements are introduced; its local-bases theorem is not applied.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1); square-zero inverse correction in the sheaf module category

proof.text: Given a current basis and an arbitrary next-level basis, descend the latter through the actual scalar cokernels. Their universal properties give the descended isomorphism and its transition equation. Compare it to the current basis, lift the resulting automorphism by Step 2, and postcompose the next-level basis with that lift. This gives a next basis satisfying the adjacent compatibility equation. Recursion starting at the prescribed residue basis gives all levels. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles the adjacent equations into a natural isomorphism of the actual towers.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1); recursion on positive reduction levels and scalar-cokernel universality

proof.text: The existing proved private free_isFiniteLocallyFree lemma from IntegralLisseTowerEffective supplies finite local freeness of the standard free sheaf, including the empty index type. A proof-only import all makes that lemma available; the effectiveness theorem is not applied. Apply the integral-lisse module completeness theorem both to N and to this standard free sheaf. Postcompose the first limit cone by the tower isomorphism from Step 3, and use uniqueness of limits to obtain an integral basis. Its projection equation, naturality of the canonical cokernel projection and epimorphy of that projection identify every actual reduction with the chosen tower basis. A separate coefficient-limit application and a separate finite-product/limit comparison are unnecessary.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1); uniqueness of limits

proof.text: For the ordinary rationalization, evaluate the integral basis on each object. Compose its linear equivalence with finite-free coordinates. The scalar-extension tensor congruence, TensorProduct.piRight and the tensor right-unit equivalence identify S(U) tensor_R(U) N(U) with the finite free S(U)-module. The resulting map sends s tensor x to coordinates s times the scalar image of the integral coordinates of x. The tensor universal property reduces naturality to pure tensors; naturality of the integral basis, free projections and the ring map proves it. Sheafify the resulting presheaf isomorphism and compose with the sheafification counit of the free target. Unit naturality and the adjunction triangle prove exactly the stated formula after the actual sheafification unit. Rank zero uses empty finite sums throughout; every construction is valid over the empty scheme without an extra hypothesis.

source.place: Definition 6.8.1 and Proposition 6.8.4(1); ordinary scalar extension and tensor sheafification

proof_origin.place: Global compatible-basis supplement to Proposition 6.8.4(1), realized by global free-generator lifts, the existing private square-zero lemmas of IntegralLisseTowerLocalBases, module completeness twice using the existing private free_isFiniteLocallyFree lemma of IntegralLisseTowerEffective, and sectionwise tensor sheafification. Both helper modules are imported proof-only with import all; none of their private lemmas is redeclared.
